clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old Caucasian female presented to the ophthalmic emergency department with a 5-day history of right eye redness, pain, blurred vision, and intermittent temporal photopsia. She also reported systemic B symptoms including long-standing night sweats, nausea, headaches, and left shoulder pain. Initial ophthalmologic examination revealed right eye non-necrotizing scleritis with anterior chamber inflammation (1+ cells), vitreous inflammation with snowballs and inferior condensations, peripheral white/yellowish retinal lesions, and papillary edema. Angiography demonstrated peripheral vasculitis with hot disc papillitis appearance. BCVA was 1.0 bilaterally. Extensive infectious and systemic disease workup was negative (toxoplasmosis, syphilis, sarcoidosis, Behçet's disease, SLE, and others). IGRA testing for tuberculosis came back positive with negative Quantiferon. PET-CT imaging revealed hypermetabolic left supraclavicular and mediastinal bilateral lymph nodes, raising differential diagnosis of lymph node tuberculosis, lymphoma, sarcoidosis, IgG4-related disease, or Castleman's disease. Lymph node biopsy confirmed nodular sclerosing Hodgkin's lymphoma stage IIB. The patient subsequently underwent 6 cycles of ABVD chemotherapy (doxorubicin, bleomycin, vinblastine, dacarbazine) with good tolerability and adherence. During treatment, BCVA remained stable at 1.0, pain resolved, but intermittent temporal right eye photopsia persisted, possibly related to chorioretinal scarring. Topical and systemic corticosteroids were maintained throughout treatment with biweekly follow-up.

final.final_diagnosis: Nodular sclerosing Hodgkin's lymphoma stage IIB with ocular manifestations (uveitis with peripheral vasculitis)
final.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old Caucasian female presented to the ophthalmic emergency department with a 5-day history of right eye redness, pain, blurred vision, and intermittent temporal photopsia. She also reported systemic B symptoms including long-standing night sweats, nausea, headaches, and left shoulder pain. Initial ophthalmologic examination revealed right eye non-necrotizing scleritis with anterior chamber inflammation (1+ cells), vitreous inflammation with snowballs and inferior condensations, peripheral white/yellowish retinal lesions, and papillary edema. Angiography demonstrated peripheral vasculitis with hot disc papillitis appearance. BCVA was 1.0 bilaterally. Extensive infectious and systemic disease workup was negative (toxoplasmosis, syphilis, sarcoidosis, Behçet's disease, SLE, and others). IGRA testing for tuberculosis came back positive with negative Quantiferon. PET-CT imaging revealed hypermetabolic left supraclavicular and mediastinal bilateral lymph nodes, raising differential diagnosis of lymph node tuberculosis, lymphoma, sarcoidosis, IgG4-related disease, or Castleman's disease. Lymph node biopsy confirmed nodular sclerosing Hodgkin's lymphoma stage IIB. The patient subsequently underwent 6 cycles of ABVD chemotherapy (doxorubicin, bleomycin, vinblastine, dacarbazine) with good tolerability and adherence. During treatment, BCVA remained stable at 1.0, pain resolved, but intermittent temporal right eye photopsia persisted, possibly related to chorioretinal scarring. Topical and systemic corticosteroids were maintained throughout treatment with biweekly follow-up.
